title: Jimmy Blanton joins the band
summary: Pillars hears Jimmy Blanton and brings him from Tennessee, helping him choose a bass fiddle.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: And the Andy Kirk band was broadcasting every -- every night. In the meantime, that particular summer, we were contacted by a recording company, The Vocalion Recording Company, and the Vocalion Recording Company paid for us to come to Chicago, and make a couple of recordings. Before we go on-- before I go on to that, I want to mention the fact that Jimmy Blanton had joined the band. In '37. And I had heard him that summer I had heard Jimmy Blanton that summer when he was up here visiting his aunt from Tennessee. And I had never

heard anyone play a bass like that before in my life. And it so happened that Jimmy Blanton had remembered the time when Alphonso Trent's band had played Chattanooga, he was a little kid, and he heard the Trent band and he was admiring the Trent band that he had heard back a few years before that time.

So I asked Jimmy Blanton would he like to join us. He said, yes, that he thought he'd be happy to. He said, but he wanted to go back home first, he went back home, and he went back to -- He was going to Tennessee State, then he wrote us and said that he was -- he was ready to leave, so we sent for him to come to St. Louis, and we took him down to the music store and he picked out a bass fiddle. We didn't buy it for him, we just stood for it. And that was when he bought his big fiddle.
